pattern_id: Duplicate votes prevent QC formation - inconsistent duplicate handling between reception and aggregation
description: BUG PATTERN: Duplicate votes prevent quorum certificate formation, enabling liveness attack. DESCRIPTION: The voting machine does not filter duplicate votes when receiving them, but CreateQuorumCert checks for duplicates and returns ErrCombineOverlap. This inconsistency means if a faulty replica sends the same vote twice, no quorum certificate can be formed. A malicious replica can exploit this to undermine system liveness by simply duplicating its votes. ROOT CAUSE: Inconsistent duplicate handling between vote reception and QC creation. The voting machine accepts duplicates into its collection, but the cryptographic signature combination step rejects overlapping signers. This creates a situation where enough votes are collected but they cannot be combined. LESSON: In BFT voting systems: 1) Filter duplicates at the EARLIEST point (reception), not at the final aggregation step; 2) Duplicate message handling must be consistent across all layers; 3) Consider this a potential attack vector - malicious nodes can exploit any inconsistency; 4) Test with 'twins' scenarios where replicas send duplicate/conflicting messages; 5) Validate that duplicate filtering doesn't create new attack vectors (e.g., replay attacks).
